faq: Which Squarespace plan do I need to sell?
You need a Business or Commerce plan to sell. Commerce plans have no extra Squarespace transaction fee. Plans and prices change, so we check your account and tell you which one fits before we set up.
Can you import my products from another store?

Yes. Send a CSV from Shopify, WooCommerce or another tool and we map it to Squarespace's product format, then check images and variants. Squarespace limits some fields, so a few items may need manual care.
Do you set up payments in my name?
We connect the provider inside your account, and you complete their sign-up and identity checks yourself. We never touch your bank details or passwords.
Can you set up shipping for different countries?
Yes. We create shipping zones and rates by region and add tax settings, but you confirm what you charge and what tax rules apply to you. We do not give tax advice.
desc:
Setting up a Squarespace online store means turning pages into a shop that can take payment, ship and report tax correctly. Ecom Swift LLC sets up your products, checkout, payment provider, shipping rates and order emails, then tests a real purchase from start to finish.

## What does a Squarespace online store setup cover?

A Squarespace online store setup covers everything between a product idea and a paid order: product pages, options, categories, payment connection, shipping rates, tax settings and the emails customers receive. It also includes a test order, because a checkout that has never been tried is a checkout that may fail on the first real sale.

Squarespace gives you the building blocks inside one editor. The work is in using them in the right order and with the right settings for where you sell.

## Why the selling side deserves careful setup

A store is judged at the moment of payment. If shipping appears only on the last step, if a size option is missing or if the confirmation email looks broken, buyers leave or write to ask for help. Each of those faults has a simple cause in the store settings.

Careful setup also reduces your workload after launch. Correct variants and inventory prevent overselling. Clear shipping zones stop disputes about delivery costs. A written refund routine means you know what to do when the first return arrives.

## How setup choices shape orders and revenue

Product pages carry most of the persuasion in a store. Clear photos, an accurate price and well-named options help a buyer choose without asking questions. Categories let people browse by need instead of scrolling a single long list.

Checkout choices matter just as much. Offering the payment methods your customers expect lowers friction. Showing delivery costs early removes a common reason to abandon a cart. Order emails that read well build confidence after the purchase and invite a second one.

## What a ready-to-sell Squarespace store includes

- Products with sharp photos, accurate titles, prices and clear descriptions.
- Variants such as size and color, with stock levels that match reality.
- Categories and navigation that suit how customers search.
- A payment provider connected in your own name.
- Shipping rates and zones for the places you deliver.
- Tax settings checked against your selling regions.
- Discount codes where you plan promotions.
- Order confirmation and shipping emails worded in your voice.
- Policy pages for shipping, returns and privacy.
- A completed test order, so you see what customers see.

## What we do, package by package

We add your products, set options, connect your payment provider and configure shipping and tax. The Basic package covers a small shop and a test order. Standard adds variants, styled product pages, shipping zones, a discount code, order emails and a CSV import. Premium reaches larger catalogs and adds digital or subscription items, abandoned cart emails, tracking, customer account pages and a handover.

We finish with a short guide so you can add products, process orders and issue refunds without us.

## Do and avoid when launching a shop

**Do:**
- Prepare photos and descriptions before setup begins.
- Decide your shipping and returns terms in advance.
- Check which regions you will sell to.
- Place one test order yourself on a phone.

**Avoid:**
- Launching with placeholder products or unfinished policies.
- Copying supplier descriptions word for word.
- Setting shipping rates by guesswork.
- Leaving test products visible after launch.

## Who this is for

A maker moving from craft fairs to online sales needs a first shop that works. A service business adding a few products or gift cards wants a small catalog without a new platform. A seller leaving another store builder wants products moved over with their options intact.

## What we need from you

Send your product list, photos, price and shipping details and the regions you serve. You keep your own payment provider account and connect it in your own name, and we never ask for a password. For access to the site, invite us as a contributor with the permissions needed for store settings, and remove us whenever the project ends.
